objective: Separate todo ownership from pi-swe core and isolate optional SWE/Todo UI automation behind a shared presentation-only docket kit, while preserving workflow.json authority, todo scope semantics, public commands/tools, persistence formats, lifecycle integrity, and evidence gates.

in: Characterize swe and todo command/tool behavior, authority selection, persistence, lifecycle transitions, completion evidence, UI/non-UI rendering, and restart/fork behavior.
Define explicit pi-swe-core, pi-todo, workflow-projection, and optional UI/automation adapter boundaries.
Extract shared ANSI-width, frame, scrolling, selection, keyboard, and modal mechanics into a presentation-only docket kit.
Move todo registration and ownership out of SWE core while preserving session, project, and initiative projection semantics.
Keep all workflow mutation and verification authority in SweService and all Todo mutations in their canonical backends.
Update documentation, anatomy, package registration, and compatibility tests.
out: Changing workflow.json schema or weakening evidence, independent-review, revision, locking, or permission-boundary guarantees.
Merging SWE and Todo persistence or mutation services into the shared docket kit.
Changing public swe/todo tool names, slash commands, authority scopes, state formats, or keyboard behavior.
Adding autonomous agents, worktrees, deployments, or a second workflow ledger.

constraints: Begins after provider initiatives 01-03 only in implementation order; it must not consume their domain code.
workflow.json remains sole SWE authority and SweService remains its mutation authority.
Shared UI emits intents only and has no session access, file I/O, service imports, Pi event registration, or timers.
Todo initiative projection remains an integration contract rather than Todo ownership folded into SWE core.
Preserve bounded TUI and non-TUI output, project/session/initiative scope selection, branch/fork behavior, and persistence compatibility.
Independent-review and ordinary-bash verification boundaries must remain intact.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Todo registration, persistence, and canonical mutation ownership are separated from pi-swe core behind explicit contracts.
SWE core remains sole owner of workflow lifecycle, workflow.json mutation, verification evidence, review, completion, and opt-in completion commits.
A shared presentation-only docket kit replaces duplicated formatting/modal mechanics without importing lifecycle, persistence, session, or registration code.
Existing swe/todo commands and tools, authority scopes, persistence formats, fork/restart behavior, keyboard actions, and bounded TUI/non-TUI output remain compatible.
Focused security, persistence, lifecycle, UI, and full repository qualification passes with independent review.

assessment.reason: This extension combines durable workflow authority, three Todo scopes, persistence, permission-bound verification, completion commits, and UI; separating it has broad integrity and compatibility risk.
surfaces: new pi-todo or equivalent extension boundary
unknowns: The least disruptive physical package split requires current package-discovery inspection.
Some existing shared types may need a compatibility export while consumers migrate.

practices.reason: Authority selection, formats, lifecycle, and restart semantics must be explicit before moving ownership.
Todo/SWE separation and shared UI must not blur persistence or lifecycle authority.
Evidence gates, locks, permissions, UI, and public surfaces need integrated and independent review.

obligations.text: Characterize SWE lifecycle/evidence/commit behavior and session, project, and initiative Todo selection, mutation, persistence, fork, restart, malformed-state, and bounded-output behavior before extraction.
Verify separated ownership with negative tests proving Todo cannot mutate workflow completion/verification and SWE core does not own Todo persistence or registration.
Test docket-kit ANSI width, truncation, frames, narrow widths, scrolling, empty lists, selection preservation, keyboard intents, and absence of lifecycle/session/file/service dependencies.
Run focused SWE/Todo persistence, qualification, security, command, UI, typecheck, and full repository gates, then obtain independent review of authority boundaries and compatibility.

work.title: Characterize SWE and Todo contracts and ownership

testing.approach: Extend existing lifecycle, evidence, persistence, branch, authority-selection, malformed-state, TUI, and command fixtures before moving modules.
testing.reason: The current welded implementation contains several durable behavioral contracts.

work.title: Separate Todo ownership from SWE core

testing.approach: Introduce explicit contracts and registration boundaries, preserve formats, and add cross-authority negative tests.
testing.reason: Todo should integrate with workflow projection without becoming part of SWE's mutation authority.

testing.approach: Move shared formatting/modal mechanics behind intent callbacks and retain adapter-level snapshot tests.
testing.reason: UI duplication can be removed safely only if domain and persistence dependencies are prohibited.

testing.approach: Run complete focused and repository gates, inspect authority boundaries, and obtain independent source-bound review.
testing.reason: The split is complete only when lifecycle integrity and existing surfaces remain proven.

decisions.text: Todo becomes a distinct ownership boundary while initiative Todo remains a workflow projection contract.
decisions.basis: This follows the review recommendation without introducing synchronization or a second initiative ledger.

decisions.text: Shared docket code owns presentation only.
decisions.basis: Lifecycle and persistence coupling would recreate the architecture problem in a new shared module.

risks.text: The physical split changes registration order or public discovery.
risks.mitigation: Characterize discovery and retain compatibility adapters until package registration tests pass.

risks.text: Shared UI begins owning lifecycle decisions.
risks.mitigation: Use intent-only interfaces and enforce forbidden imports in production shared UI.

risks.text: Persistence formats drift during module moves.
risks.mitigation: Use existing fixtures, byte/schema compatibility tests, and malformed-state negative cases.

risks.text: Verification or completion permission boundaries weaken.
risks.mitigation: Retain ordinary-bash observation tests and independently review mutation ownership.
